title: intent edit ignores the kind argument it was given and answers about a steel thread
body:
**MEASURED 2026-08-29 by ic against the debug binary, immediately after the AC-17.6 shape change landed in the register.**

```
intent edit issue 148 --path   ->  rc=1   error: no steel thread ST0148 in this project
```

The row declares `kind` with values `st | wp | issue` (AC-17.6: the kind is what disambiguates, because `intent edit 1` already refuses with `1 names both a steel thread and an issue`). **The parser accepts `issue`, the arm ignores it, and the refusal is about a steel thread the caller never named.**

**This is the same class as the defect the shape change was written to remove.** `intent edit st 68` used to parse `st` as the address and `68` as the file, and refuse about the wrong thing. It now parses correctly and still refuses about the wrong thing, one layer in -- the disambiguator is read by clap and dropped before resolution.

**It is worse than a missing feature because the operator supplied the answer.** A caller who types `issue` has already resolved the ambiguity the tool reports; being told about `ST0148` says the tool discarded the one piece of information it asked for.

**The register records it rather than hiding it:** `declared_values_are_enforced.rs` refuses a `values` slot with no stated disposition, so `edit.kind` is dispositioned `Unenforced` against this issue number. `Unenforced` is a disposition and not an exemption -- it pins the defect to a referent, and the row moves to `Enforced` when the resolver reads the kind.

**Owed by WP-17 piece 3** (the realisers), or sooner if anyone touches the edit arm first.
